subject: Stratus commercial clarifications & proposed action plan
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@stratus.ai>

Cc: Michael Stone <michael.stone@stratus.ai>, procurement@stratus.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redlines + commercial questions (Order Form v3)

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached is our redlined order form (Stratus_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.pdf). A few commercial points we want to align on before legal does a final pass: 

1) Pricing schedule: the tiers on page 2 look good, but we need confirmation on when tiered pricing kicks in (calendar quarter vs billing month).
2) Minimum commit: we flagged the ramp schedule — can Redwood confirm whether usage shortfalls will be credited or invoiced as a true-up?
3) Net terms: Stratus typically pushes net30 for startups, but for enterprise deals we prefer net45. Can you confirm Redwood's flexibility?
4) Invoicing cadence & entity: we have two billing entities (Stratus US and Stratus EU). Want to confirm invoices can be split and assigned to separate POs.
5) Taxes: please confirm which party is responsible for withholding and whether Redwood will accept VAT reverse-charge where applicable.

Also need an estimated turnaround for your legal/finance review; customer legal wants a signature route within 5 business days if possible.

Attached: Stratus_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Procurement Lead 
Stratus AI
alyssa.chen@stratus.ai

--

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@stratus.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial redlines + commercial questions (Order Form v3)

Alyssa —

Appreciate the clear redlines and list. High level answers and a proposed action plan below so we move quickly: 

- Pricing kick-in: Redwood prefers month-of-billing triggers, but we can accept quarter-alignment if you need predictable revenue recognition. Please confirm which you prefer; we'll update the schedule accordingly.
- Minimum commit true-up: Our standard is a quarterly true-up invoiced in arrears; exceptions possible with an upfront credit.
- Net terms: Finance prefers net45 for enterprise deals (we can provisionally accept net45 here), pending final credit check.
- Split invoicing: We can issue separate invoices to different legal entities; we'll need separate PO numbers and remit addresses.
- Taxes: Customer is generally responsible for VAT/withholding; we'll accept reverse-charge where legally applicable, but need local tax evidence.

Proposed timeline: legal review (Markus) today/tomorrow, finance confirmation of net45 by EOD Monday, and DocuSign envelope to you by end of next business day after legal sign-off.

Next steps I’ll take now: loop in Legal + Finance (cc'd). Please confirm if you require quarter-based pricing trigger — I’ll mark that as the only open commercial input from your side.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales 
Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal — Stratus order form: commercial asks and proposed edits (please advise)

Team —

Forwarding Stratus's redlines (see original below). Quick summary of commercial points to resolve: 

1) Pricing trigger: customer prefers quarter; they flagged forecasting reasons. Our default is month. If Finance will accept quarter-trigger we keep litigation/system simplicity on their side. Karthik — input?

2) Min-commit treatment: Recommend quarterly true-up invoice in arrears. If Legal requires changes to termination/credit language, suggest a narrow amendment to Section 4 (payment / true-up) rather than rewriting the ramp schedule.

3) Net terms: Finance has historically accepted net45 for enterprise accounts — Kimberly, can you confirm whether net45 is OK to extend to Stratus pending credit clearance?

4) Taxes & invoicing split: We will accept reverse-charge where local law supports it but require the customer's tax certificate and remit instructions. Also need process for issuing two invoices across entities (POs).

5) Limit of liability & indemnity: Markus, I flagged two clauses where Stratus proposed expanding our liability exposure — please propose redline language that preserves the spirit of the offer but keeps our cap and indemnity carveouts intact.

Deliverables: Markus to send suggested Order Form amendments today; Kimberly to confirm net terms and invoice split process by Monday; I will draft a 1-page commercials summary for the customer and prepare DocuSign once we have legal language.

Thanks,
Vivek

Vivek / team —

I reviewed Stratus's redlines and have a concise set of suggested edits attached (Redwood_Suggested_Amendments_OrderForm_v1.docx). Highlights: 

1) Liability cap: keep current cap at 12 months of fees with an explicit carveout for gross negligence / willful misconduct. Propose precise language at Section 7(b).
2) Taxes & withholding: counter-propose customer responsible for withholding; Redwood will support VAT reverse-charge where verifiable, but need customer-supplied tax certificates before issuance of credit notes.
3) Net terms: acceptable to mark Net45 in Order Form; include a standard credit hold clause if delinquent beyond 60 days.
4) Invoicing split: add appendix to specify invoice remittance details for multiple legal entities; require separate PO numbers.

If everyone signs off, I can incorporate these and prepare a redline to send back to Stratus. I will not expand indemnity language as requested — propose an alternative narrow remedy cap.

Attachment: Redwood_Suggested_Amendments_OrderForm_v1.docx (docx)
